title: Three groups. One ring.
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: All three substituents are on the same face. A chair flip changes axial/equatorial positions but preserves every stereocenter.
task: Name the compound, assign R/S, count stereoisomers and look down both indicated ring bonds.

title: A five-membered twist
subtitle: Newman studio
takeaway: The methyl and chlorine are trans. A five-membered ring puckers; a flat pentagon is only a connectivity drawing.
task: Identify the two stereocenters, then sight down each arrowed bond.

title: Look straight down the bond
subtitle: Newman studio
takeaway: The alcohol gives the parent chain its numbering: 4-bromoheptan-3-ol. Both substituted carbons are stereocenters.
task: Put the bromine-bearing carbon in front when looking toward the alcohol-bearing carbon.

title: The bulky-group anchor
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: The tert-butyl group strongly favors an equatorial position. The two alcohols are trans and exchange diaxial and diequatorial arrangements on flipping.
task: Name and assign the stereocenters. Compare the two indicated Newman views.

title: Meet your mirror image
subtitle: Stereoisomer studio
takeaway: Butane-2,3-diol has three stereoisomers. RR and SS are enantiomers; each is a diastereomer of the achiral meso form.
task: Compare all three Fischer projections. Horizontal bonds point toward you; vertical bonds point away.

title: Find the all-equatorial chair
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: Both methyl groups and chlorine can be equatorial simultaneously. Keep the wedge/dash faces fixed as you flip.
task: Find the lowest-strain chair, inspect the two Newman axes and assign each stereocenter.

title: A small axial compromise
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: Trans-1,3 substitution requires one axial group. The slender nitrile can be axial while the amino group is equatorial.
task: Compare chairs and look down the arrowed bonds. The nitrile carbon is linear, not tetrahedral.

title: Two rings, one locked hinge
subtitle: Decalin workshop
takeaway: Trans-decalin cannot perform an ordinary chair flip: the fused ring locks the junction. Cis-decalin can interconvert between chair-chair conformations.
task: Compare the bridgehead hydrogens. Same face is cis; opposite faces are trans. Rotate to see the ring junction.

title: A charge with room to roam
subtitle: Electron playground
takeaway: Adjacent π bonds can donate toward the carbocation. The positive charge is delocalized across the conjugated system; the sigma skeleton stays fixed.
task: Step through contributors and follow the electron-pair arrows. Start every arrow at a bond or a lone pair.

title: Let oxygen carry the charge
subtitle: Electron playground
takeaway: The enediolate and carbonyl are conjugated. Oxygen-bearing contributors stabilize negative charge while retaining complete octets.
task: Follow donation from the O⁻ lone pair into the ring and then toward the carbonyl.

title: A lone pair joins the ring
subtitle: Electron playground
takeaway: The hydroxyl oxygen can donate a lone pair when the cation reaches its carbon. The resulting oxonium contributor gives that carbon a full octet.
task: Trace the cation around the ring, then identify the contributor with a positive oxygen.

title: Cis wins this round
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: Cis-1,3 allows both groups to be equatorial. For the less stable trans isomer, keep methyl equatorial and chlorine axial.
task: Compare cis and trans, including the better chair of the trans isomer.

title: Fit three groups around the ring
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: All three groups can be equatorial. Its mirror image has the same energy in an achiral environment.
task: Find the all-equatorial arrangement and compare its enantiomer. Toggle R/S labels to inspect the three centers.

title: A three-center balancing act
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: The all-equatorial stereoisomer avoids axial methyl groups. Reflecting all three centers produces its equally stable enantiomer.
task: Assign the stereocenters in both members of the lowest-strain enantiomeric pair.

title: Give tert-butyl some space
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: Flipping places tert-butyl equatorial. Its strong axial penalty outweighs the cost of axial isopropyl and nitrile groups.
task: Read up/down faces in the flat map. Then flip the original chair and compare which groups become axial.

title: Keep the faces, swap the seats
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: These groups are trans-1,3. A flip preserves that relationship and exchanges which group is axial. Standard axial penalties favor equatorial NH₂.
task: Convert the original chair to wedges and dashes, then inspect the flipped chair and its stereocenters.

title: Two methyls outweigh one isopropyl
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: Keeping both methyl groups equatorial can outweigh the axial cost of one isopropyl group. The mirror has identical steric preferences.
task: Compare the two chairs. Inspect the enantiomer of the original, lower-strain chair.

title: A sugar in three dimensions
subtitle: Conformation lab
takeaway: This is the six-membered pyranose form of D-ribose. The original chair has three equatorial OH groups and one axial OH; flipping reverses that count.
task: Track all four stereocenters. Ring oxygen is part of the ring and is not a stereocenter.

title: The architecture of estrone
subtitle: Stereocenter hunt
takeaway: Estrone has four tetrahedral stereocenters. The aromatic carbons and carbonyl carbon are planar and do not count. The formal configurational maximum is 16.
task: Click atoms to identify the four stereocenters. Compare the whole molecule with its mirror.

title: Vitamin C, without the flatness
subtitle: Stereocenter hunt
takeaway: Ascorbic acid has two stereocenters and four configurational stereoisomers. The enediol carbons are sp² and are not stereocenters.
task: Find the ring stereocenter and the side-chain stereocenter. Notice where the molecule becomes planar.

title: Two centers. Still achiral.
subtitle: Symmetry studio
takeaway: The symmetric 3,5-diol shown is meso. Opposite configurations are related by the molecule’s internal symmetry; there are three distinct stereoisomers.
task: Compare the meso molecule, its reflection and a chiral diastereomer. Two stereocenters do not automatically make a molecule chiral.

title: Protonate, then follow the electrons
subtitle: Acid + resonance
takeaway: Explore ring-carbon protonation and the resulting delocalized cation. This is one illustrative protonation pathway; the carboxyl group also offers protonation sites.
task: Follow a ring π pair toward H⁺, break H–Cl toward Cl⁻, then compare the charged contributors.
acidNote: Illustrative α-carbon protonation, not a prediction of a unique product or protonation site.

title: One nitrogen takes the proton
subtitle: Acid + resonance
takeaway: Protonate the pyridine-like nitrogen, which has the available lone pair. Imidazolium delocalizes the positive charge while preserving aromatic stabilization.
task: Identify the nitrogen without H in the starting molecule, then inspect the protonated resonance contributors.
